labels.label: cor:gap-nonneg

hypotheses.paper: the leaf (Σ_t, g_t) is closed, N ≥ 3
hypotheses.note: measured model with n = 0 (DEC-186, kb/0088); 3 ≤ N; compact as IsFiniteMeasure vol_g; hD (D measurable) as the strict library

hypotheses.paper: constant R_{g_t} ≤ 0, or more generally g_t a Yamabe metric
hypotheses.note: (∃ c ≤ 0, R = c vol_g-a.e.) ∨ EH(g) = Y(g); the first branch reduces to the second by prop:csc-yamabe (a) (strict csc_yamabe_a)

hypotheses.paper: σ(Σ) = sup over all conformal classes
hypotheses.note: OQ-132 (b): over a supplied family rep of class representatives (yamabeClasses), bounded above (hb: Aubin's bound, thm:yamabe (a), not formalized); the class of g in the family (hC₀ : Y(rep C₀) = Y(g)). gapNonneg_core needs only Y(g) ≤ σ
ExtremalA σ Einstein g, at g, the σ ≤ 0 branch only; Einstein a supplied predicate (no Ricci tensor on the model)

hypotheses.paper: « in dimension three Einstein metrics have constant sectional curvature » (l.243)
hypotheses.note: EinsteinConstCurv3 Einstein ConstCurv g; not named in the dispatch, but the model has no curvature tensor, so it cannot be proved

hypotheses.paper: thm:extremal (b): σ = R_{g0} Vol(g0)^{2/N} when Σ is hyperbolic 3-dim, flat, S^N or RP^3
hypotheses.note: hB at a metric g0 of constant scalar curvature R0; the diffeomorphism type has no counterpart in the model

findings: l.244: « rescaling g_0 to volume V_i gives k = R_{g_0} »: the identity holds for the rescaled metric g_0' = (V_i/Vol(g_0))^{2/N} g_0, which the proof keeps calling g_0; for g_0 itself k = R_{g_0} (Vol(g_0)/V_i)^{2/N}. Notational, no correction of substance (cor_gap_nonneg_b states it for g_0').
questions: « g_t attains the Yamabe invariant » (l.236) is read as « g_t is a Yamabe metric and Y(Σ,[g_t]) = σ(Σ) » (thm:extremal (a)'s phrasing, l.209); under the corollary's hypothesis it is equivalent to EH(Σ_t, g_t) = σ(Σ), and both equivalences with δ = 0 are proved.

(b) « the FLRW model whose leaf at time t_i has constant curvature and volume V_i » is read as the family a² g_0' with g_0' the rescaling of thm:extremal (b)'s g_0 to volume V_i; « constant curvature » of g_0' is read through its constant scalar curvature, and « curvature term » as −⟨R⟩ of that leaf in eq:accel. The homothety's scaling laws R ↦ R/l, H ↦ H/√l are the definition of CurvedMetric.homothety (the model cannot derive them).
The readings of OQ-132 are taken (σ over a supplied family; Σ not assumed connected).

labels.label: cor:volume

hypotheses.paper: Σ a closed hyperbolic 3-manifold, g_hyp its hyperbolic metric
hypotheses.note: measured model with N = 3, n = 0; « hyperbolic » as the supplied ConstCurv g_hyp with R_{g_hyp} ≡ c
∀ x, g.R x = c, ∀ x, g_hyp.R x = c, c < 0
OQ-132 (b), as for cor:gap-nonneg (family, hb, hC₀)
MostowAt ConstCurv Isometric g g_hyp; Isometric a supplied relation

hypotheses.paper: isometric ⇒ equal volume (the « if » half of the equality case, not argued in the paper)

findings: l.255: the proof writes « attain σ(Σ) < 0 »; only σ(Σ) ≤ 0 is used (for thm:extremal (a)). The « if » half of « equality if and only if isometric » (isometric metrics have equal volume) is not argued; trivial on manifolds, carried here.
questions: R_{g_hyp} is any negative constant (the statement does not normalise the hyperbolic metric to sectional curvature −1); read so, ghyp any metric with ConstCurv and R ≡ c < 0.
Connectedness (OQ-132 (a)) is not assumed: the inequality and the carried Mostow input hold componentwise.

kb_proposals: A homothety on the measured model: CurvedMetric.homothety l hl g (G ↦ l•G, R ↦ R/l, H ↦ H/√l as data); vol_{lg} = ofReal(l^{N/2}) • vol_g by sqrt_det_smul and withDensity_smul' (no measurability needed); closed EH is then homothety-invariant (Yamabe scaffold GapCorollaries).

A cited theorem about a notion the model lacks (Einstein, constant sectional curvature, isometry): supply the notion as a predicate argument and carry the cited implication at the metric where the paper invokes it (ExtremalA, EinsteinConstCurv3, MostowAt); disclose that with the predicate True the conclusion is trivial (kb/0095).
